subject: Helix on-prem deployment: throughput commitments & handoff items
messages:
From: Sara Ahmed <sara.ahmed@helixanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput commitments for Helix on-prem deployment

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. We're trying to lock the numbers for procurement and need a crisp summary of the throughput and latency guarantees Redwood can commit to for our on-prem VPC deployment. A few specifics we need to include in the SOW:

- Expected sustained QPS and peak burst QPS for the recommended configuration (assume avg request = 120 tokens).
- 95th and 99th percentile latency targets for text-generation (single-turn, 512 token cap).
- Warm-up time and cache-warm strategies (how long until prefix/KV cache reaches steady state).
- Network egress/bandwidth requirements per GPU node and any firewall/NAT considerations.
- Anything we should surface to our infra team (NFS/kv-store, kernel tuning, MTU).

We are targeting a go-live window in mid-November and procurement needs the estimate + SLA language by next Friday. Can you include a simple ops handoff checklist we can attach to the procurement packet?

Appreciate it,
Sara
Sara Ahmed
Head of Platform, Helix Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Ahmed <sara.ahmed@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput commitments for Helix on-prem deployment

Sara —

Summary below (high level). I've attached an initial estimate workbook, a network diagram, and a draft SLA for your procurement team. If this aligns, we'll turn it into formal SOW language.

Quick numbers (recommended initial configuration):
- Baseline: 4 x A100-80GB nodes (dedicated pool)
- Sustained throughput: ~90 requests/sec (avg 120 tokens/request) at median token-per-second scheduling
- Peak burst capacity (short): 220 requests/sec for up to 10 minutes (autoscale + burst nodes)
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 220 ms, 99th <= 420 ms (single-turn, 512 token cap)
- Warm cache: typical steady-state cache hit-rate within 30–45 minutes of steady traffic; prefix caching can reduce per-request GPU time by ~25–35% depending on prompt overlap

Operational notes:
- Autoscale policy: add 1 node when GPU util > 70% for 4 consecutive minutes; remove when < 40% for 10 minutes. We recommend keeping 1 warm standby node for faster cold-start absorption.
- KV cache: requires an NFS or local SSD-backed KV store with sustained ~1GB/s sequential throughput for the working set. We suggest a 10TB NVMe aggregate with raid across nodes in your clustered storage.
- Network: recommend 25 Gbps NICs on each node, BGP/NAT egress rules to permit outbound control plane + model pulls (we documented ports in the attached diagram).
- Monitoring: token-level cost/latency traces and an ops playbook for fallbacks (route to hosted model if local pool saturated).

I'll note two tradeoffs for procurement: we can reduce reserved nodes if Helix accepts a 99.8% latency SLA rather than 99.95% (saves ~20% on committed capacity).

Attachments: helix_estimate_v1.xlsx, network_egress_diagram.png, SLA_proposal_helix.pdf

Next steps: if this looks good, procurement can sign the quoted SOW and we'll schedule a joint ops runbook session with your infra team.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput commitments for Helix on-prem deployment

Rishi — quick internal notes before we finalize the SOW: 

- The baseline numbers look reasonable but recommend we include a 25% conservative headroom buffer for the first 90 days (customer traffic patterns often differ). Call it "initial stabilization buffer" in the SOW.
- For NVMe/KV: confirm whether they will provide on-prem storage or if Redwood will supply an appliance. That impacts lead time and pricing.
- Network egress: call out recommended egress cap per node (we should say 5 Gbps sustained with 25 Gbps burst) and include a note about MTU=9000 where possible.
- Add a sentence on model version pinning and fallback policy (if model update causes regressions we fall back to version X and notify Helix).

I'll patch the workbook after Rishi confirms the storage ownership and the exact autoscale thresholds.

-Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput commitments for Helix on-prem deployment

Marissa / Laura —

Answers inline: 
- Headroom buffer: agree. We'll add 25% initial stabilization buffer for the first 90 days and schedule a capacity review at 60 days.
- Storage ownership: Helix prefers to use their own on-prem NVMe farm; they confirmed they have ~12TB available per rack node. We'll call this out and include a Redwood-managed fallback option (appliance) as an add-on.
- Egress numbers: confirmed — document 5 Gbps sustained per node, allow 25 Gbps burst for model pulls/evictions. Also include guidance to enable jumbo frames (MTU 9000).
- SLA trade: reaffirming that 99.8% vs 99.95% latency band materially impacts committed pool size — note included in margin table in the workbook.

I'll update the attached sheet to include the 25% buffer and a simple ops handoff checklist (runbooks, escalation matrix, playbook for cold cache).

Rishi
